sandbox.title: Interactive Simulation Room
sandbox.description: Pick an elementary math topic below — click to plant seeds, grab candy, share apples — and watch formulas change in real time!

multiplication.title: Multiplication: 3 plates, each with 4 strawberry candies
multiplication.explanation: Multiplication is essentially adding groups of equal size repeatedly. Instead of writing 4 + 4 + 4, you can write 3 × 4.
multiplication.lifeExample: Imagine mom prepares 3 clean plates. On each plate, she neatly places 4 sweet strawberry candies. Let's count how many candies we have in total!
multiplication.question: In the garden, Brown Rabbit planted 4 rows of sweet carrots. Each row has exactly 5 round plump carrots. Which multiplication shows the total number of carrots?
multiplication.correctMsg: Wonderful! The rabbit harvested 20 delicious carrots!
multiplication.incorrectMsg: Not quite, sweetie! There are 4 groups (4 rows), each with 5 carrots — so 4 × 5 = 20!

division.title: Division: Share 12 red apples equally among 3 dolls
division.explanation: Division is about distributing a quantity equally into parts — so every doll gets a fair share.
division.lifeExample: You have 12 crisp red apples. You want to share them equally among 3 adorable plush dolls standing in line. How many apples does each friend get?
division.question: The teacher has 15 notebooks. He wants to share them equally among 5 outstanding students. How many notebooks does each student receive?
division.correctMsg: Exactly! 15 notebooks shared among 5 friends — each gets 3 beautiful notebooks!
division.incorrectMsg: Not quite! Try dividing 15 equally among 5 groups — each group gets 3.

fraction.title: Fractions: Eating 3 slices of a pizza cut into 4
fraction.explanation: A fraction shows equal parts of a whole. The denominator (bottom) is the total number of slices. The numerator (top) is how many slices are eaten.
fraction.lifeExample: Mom bakes a delicious strawberry pizza and cuts it evenly into 4 slices. A hungry child happily eats all 3 slices. The fraction for the eaten part is 3/4!
fraction.question: A long strip of paper is divided into 6 equal segments like a ruler. Mai colors 5 segments green. Which fraction represents the part Mai colored?
fraction.correctMsg: Excellent! The colored pieces (5) go on top, the total pieces (6) go on the bottom — making 5/6!
fraction.incorrectMsg: Oops! Remember: the selected parts go on top as the numerator, and the total parts go on the bottom as the denominator.

area.title: Area & Perimeter: A garden plot 4m long and 3m wide
area.explanation: Perimeter is the total distance around the edges. Area is the entire flat green surface inside, covered with grass squares.
area.lifeExample: Dad fences a small garden plot 4 meters long and 3 meters wide — for the child to grow flowers. The planting area is 12 square meters, and the fence perimeter is 14 meters.
area.question: Mom gives you a rectangular study mat that is 5dm long and 4dm wide. Calculate the perimeter and area of this mat!
area.incorrectMsg: Almost! Area = Length × Width (5 × 4), and Perimeter = (Length + Width) × 2.

roadmap.title: Visual roadmap — Grades 1 through 5
roadmap.description: Every lesson is supported by haptic visual diagrams — helping children learn effortlessly from counting to calculating perimeter and area of complex polygons.
roadmap.grade1Desc: Arrange number sequences, add and subtract from 1 to 10 — based on ripe fruits, dot patterns comparing more and less.
roadmap.grade2Desc: Build equal plate arrangements — deeply understand that multiplication is repeated addition, division is equal sharing.
roadmap.grade3Desc: Children learn basic fractions, multi-digit multiplication — through stacking toy blocks.
roadmap.grade4Desc: Calculate square meters of tiles, trace wall edges. Count area in a very direct way.
roadmap.grade5Desc: Pour juice into graduated cylinders — to intuit percentages and box volume.

faq.title: Common Questions from Parents
faq.description: Quick answers to the most common concerns about using an interactive AI tutor for children.
faq.q1: Will my child get addicted and lazy about doing real homework?
faq.a1: Absolutely NOT! The system doesn't lock assignments or fill in answers. The AI's main job is to visualize math concepts — from candy plates to pizza slices — to stimulate thinking. Then the child still has to reason and solve problems on their own.
faq.q2: Does this visual curriculum follow Vietnam's Ministry of Education standards?
faq.a2: Yes, the roadmap is carefully aligned with the new General Education Curriculum. All Grade 1-5 milestones — from addition tables, grouped multiplication, fractions to perimeter and area — are 100% compatible with current textbooks.
faq.q3: What's the biggest benefit of the narrated voice feature (Speaker)?
faq.a3: For 1st and 2nd graders, reading comprehension is still limited. The Vietnamese voice narration guides children to listen and learn independently — without feeling lonely or needing parents beside them.
faq.q4: How can I get the best results from this feature?
faq.a4: Let your child take control! Encourage them to click and drag pizza slices, tap soil squares to plant seeds on screen. Hands-on haptic interaction always sparks optimal thinking patterns in young minds.
